extracted.intended_audience: national competent authorities (IP offices), WIPO officials, legal practitioners, and beneficiaries/producers of appellations of origin and geographical indications
extracted.subtask_short: international registration of GIs and AOs
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/substantive standards for the international registration, protection, modification, refusal, and administration of appellations of origin and geographical indications under the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement (2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of appellation of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Any denomination protected in the Contracting Party of Origin consisting of or containing the name of a geographical area, or another denomination known as referring to such area, which serves to designate a good as originating in that geographical area, where the quality or characteristics of the good are due exclusively or essentially to the geographical environment, including natural and human factors, and which has given the good its reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive threshold for an appellation of origin: (i) denomination referencing a geographical area; (ii) quality/characteristics due exclusively or essentially to geographical environment (natural + human factors); (iii) denomination has given the good its reputation. These elements determine eligibility under Article 2(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of geographical indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Any indication protected in the Contracting Party of Origin consisting of or containing the name of a geographical area, or another indication known as referring to such area, which identifies a good as originating in that geographical area, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic of the good is essentially attributable to its geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differs from 'appellation of origin' by wording: protection where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to geographical origin (Article 2(1)(ii)). Use this to assess whether an indication qualifies as a GI rather than an AO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible geographical areas of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical area of origin may consist of the entire territory of the Contracting Party of Origin or a region, locality or place in the Contracting Party of Origin; includes trans-border geographical areas or a part thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographical area can be broad (whole state) or narrow (locality) and may be trans-border; eligibility analyses must account for these permutations (Article 2(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Competent Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall designate an entity which shall be responsible for the administration of this Act in its territory and for communications with the International Bureau under this Act and the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of name and contact details of the Competent Authority to the International Bureau is required as specified in the Regulations (Article 3). Competent Authority is the filing/communication channel and administrator domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Register maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall maintain an International Register recording international registrations effected under this Act, under the Lisbon Agreement and the 1967 Act, or under both, and data relating to such international registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register is the official collection of data concerning international registrations regardless of medium; International Bureau must publish entries and maintain records (Article 4 and multiple Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of filing (application locus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be filed with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct filing with International Bureau is the default procedure (Article 5(1)); Regulations specify mandatory particulars. National filing routes are governed by designation/declarations (Article 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for international registration shall be filed by the Competent Authority in the name of (i) the beneficiaries; or (ii) a natural person or legal entity having legal standing under the law of the Contracting Party of Origin to assert the rights of the beneficiaries or other rights in the appellation of origin or geographical indication; where domestic law permits, beneficiaries or such persons may file directly subject to a declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint applications are possible for trans-border areas through a commonly designated Competent Authority. Declarations by Contracting Parties (at ratification/accession or later) permit direct filing by beneficiaries; effective dates vary (Article 5(2)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and optional application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations shall specify the mandatory particulars that must be included in the application, in addition to those specified in Article 6(3). The Regulations may specify optional particulars that may be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and Competent Authorities must consult the Regulations for required particulars (Article 5(5)-(6)); missing particulars affect date of registration under Article 6(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination and registration by International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an application for the international registration of an appellation of origin or a geographical indication in due form, as specified in the Regulations, the International Bureau shall register the appellation of origin, or the geographical indication, in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau performs formal (not substantive) examination for due form per Regulations before entering the Register (Article 6(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of international registration (and effect of missing particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of the international registration shall be the date on which the application was received by the International Bureau; where certain particulars (identification of Competent Authority/applicant, details identifying beneficiaries, the appellation/indication itself, and the goods concerned) are missing, the date is the date on which the last missing particular is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects priority and the date from which protection and refusal deadlines run. Ensure all particulars are supplied to secure earliest possible date (Article 6(2)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification of international registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, without delay, publish each international registration and notify the Competent Authority of each Contracting Party of the international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers rights and procedural timelines in Contracting Parties and starts periods for possible refusals and notifications (Article 6(4); Rule 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of effect of protection and Contracting Party declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered appellation of origin or geographical indication shall, in each Contracting Party that has not refused protection in accordance with Article 15, or that has sent to the International Bureau a notification of grant of protection in accordance with Article 18, be protected from the date of the international registration; a Contracting Party may declare protection to start from a specified date not later than the expiry of the time limit for refusal specified in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Parties can notify an earlier/later date of protection subject to limits; consult Regulations for refusal time limits. Declarations change domestic effect timing (Article 6(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International registration fees and other fees
rubrics_metrics.description: International registration of each appellation of origin, and each geographical indication, shall be subject to payment of the fee specified in the Regulations. The Regulations shall specify fees for other entries and for extracts, attestations, or other information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees fund the Special Union; fee scales, reductions and particulars are set by Assembly and Regulations (Article 7(1)-(2); Rule 8 referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions (developing/LDCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced fees shall be established by the Assembly in respect of certain international registrations, in particular those in respect of which the Contracting Party of Origin is a developing country or a least-developed country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly may adopt preferential fee treatments; beneficiaries from developing/LDC Contracting Parties may benefit (Article 7(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual fee required by a Contracting Party
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting Party may notify that protection resulting from international registration shall extend to it only if a fee is paid to cover its cost of substantive examination; amount indicated in declaration may not exceed equivalent national/regional amount diminished by savings resulting from the international procedure; non-payment effects renunciation in accordance with the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows Contracting Parties to recover domestic substantive-examination costs; failure to pay an individual fee results in protection being renounced for that Contracting Party (Article 7(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of validity of international registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: International registrations shall be valid indefinitely, on the understanding that protection of a registered appellation of origin or geographical indication shall no longer be required if the denomination or indication is no longer protected in the Contracting Party of Origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validity is dependent on continued protection in Contracting Party of Origin; domestic lapse in origin triggers requirement to cancel international registration (Article 8(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of international registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Competent Authority of the Contracting Party of Origin, or (in Article 5(3) cases) the beneficiaries or authorized person or the Competent Authority, may at any time request the International Bureau to cancel the international registration concerned; where denomination/indication is no longer protected in the Contracting Party of Origin, Competent Authority shall request cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation may be requested at any time; International Bureau records cancellation and communicates to other Competent Authorities (Article 8(2); Rule 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to protect registered AOs and GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall protect registered appellations of origin and geographical indications on its territory, within its own legal system and practice but in accordance with the terms of this Act, subject to any refusal, renunciation, invalidation or cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Parties with laws that do not distinguish AOs and GIs are not required to introduce such a distinction; protection must be consistent with Act's terms (Article 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of legal protection is discretionary but must meet substantive requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall be free to choose the type of legislation under which it establishes the protection stipulated in this Act, provided that such legislation meets the substantive requirements of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility (e.g., trademark law, sui generis GI law) so long as substantive protections (Article 11 etc.) are implemented (Article 10(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to other instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Act shall not affect other protection a Contracting Party may accord under its national/regional legislation or other international instruments, nor derogate from obligations under other instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act sits alongside other rights; conflicts are managed so as not to impair other protections (Article 10(2)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of protection — prohibited uses (same kind goods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall provide the legal means to prevent use of the appellation of origin or the geographical indication in respect of goods of the same kind as those to which the appellation or indication applies, not originating in the geographical area of origin or not complying with any other applicable requirements for using the appellation or indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection aims to prevent misrepresentation of origin and non-compliant use on same-kind goods (Article 11(1)(a)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of protection — prohibited uses (different goods/services; dilution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent use in respect of goods not of the same kind or services if such use would indicate or suggest a connection with beneficiaries and be likely to damage their interests, or because of reputation, likely to impair or dilute in an unfair manner, or take unfair advantage of, that reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers 'dilution'/'taking advantage' by use on dissimilar goods/services where reputation would be exploited or harmed (Article 11(1)(a)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against misleading practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall provide the legal means to prevent any other practice liable to mislead consumers as to the true origin, provenance or nature of the goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad consumer-protection standard that complements origin-specific prohibitions (Article 11(1)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection applies to imitation and translated/qualified uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection applies to use amounting to imitation even if true origin is indicated, or if the appellation/indication is used in translated form or accompanied by terms such as 'style','kind','type','make','imitation','method','as produced in','like','similar' or the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-evasion rule: adding qualifiers or translations does not avoid infringement (Article 11(2)). Agreed statement clarifies protection need not cover components generic in Contracting Party of Origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on trademark registration and on later trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party shall, ex officio if legislation permits or at the request of an interested party, refuse or invalidate the registration of a later trademark if use of the trademark would result in a prohibited situation under Article 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GIs/AOs can be grounds to refuse or invalidate later trademarks that would create the prohibited uses described in Article 11(1)-(2), subject to prior rights exceptions (Article 11(3) and Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against becoming generic
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the provisions of this Act, registered appellations of origin and registered geographical indications cannot be considered to have become generic in a Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 12 establishes non-genericity; Agreed Statement clarifies this is without prejudice to prior use where, prior to international registration, the denomination may already have been generic in another Contracting Party (Article 12 and agreed statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard — prior trademark rights and good faith acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of this Act shall not prejudice a prior trademark applied for or registered in good faith, or acquired through use in good faith, in a Contracting Party; where limited exceptions exist in national law they apply as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior trademarks in good faith are protected; where domestic law allows exceptions, such exceptions limit interplay between trademarks and GI protection (Article 13(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard — personal names used in business
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act shall not prejudice the right of any person to use, in the course of trade, that person's name or predecessor's name, except where such use is used so as to mislead the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal name usage is protected unless it misleads; fits balance between individual and collective GI rights (Article 13(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard — plant variety or animal breed denominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act shall not prejudice the right to use a plant variety or animal breed denomination in the course of trade, except where such use is used so as to mislead the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar carve-out for plant/animal variety names; prevents overlap with other denomination systems (Article 13(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard where prior-right-based refusal is later withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Contracting Party that has refused an international registration on the ground of use under a prior trademark or other right notifies the withdrawal of that refusal or a grant of protection, resulting protection shall not prejudice that right or its use unless protection was granted following cancellation/non-renewal/revocation/invalidity of that right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves legal certainty for holders of prior rights when a refusal is withdrawn or protection granted (Article 13(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedures and remedies availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall make available effective legal remedies for the protection of registered appellations of origin and registered geographical indications and provide that legal proceedings may be brought by a public authority or by any interested party, depending on its legal system and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires accessible judicial/administrative remedies and standing for public authorities or interested parties (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of effects — timing, grounds, and who may notify
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the time limit specified in the Regulations, the Competent Authority of a Contracting Party may notify the International Bureau of the refusal of the effects of an international registration in its territory; notification may be made ex officio if legislation permits or at the request of an interested party, and must set out the grounds for refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal deadlines are set in the Regulations; Competent Authorities must state grounds; interested parties must be given a reasonable opportunity to request that Competent Authority to notify refusal (Article 15(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, publication and communication of refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall record the refusal and the grounds in the International Register, publish the refusal and communicate the notification to the Competent Authority of the Contracting Party of Origin or, where appropriate, the beneficiaries or applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency obligation; refusal entries are published and communicated to origin/beneficiaries (Article 15(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: National treatment for remedies against refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting Party shall make available to interested parties affected by a refusal the same judicial and administrative remedies that are available to its own nationals in respect of the refusal of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures equality of procedural remedies for foreign interested parties (Article 15(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of refusal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal may be withdrawn in accordance with the procedures specified in the Regulations and a withdrawal shall be recorded in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent Authorities can reverse prior refusals by following Regulations; International Bureau records withdrawal (Article 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to grant transitional periods to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Contracting Party has not refused effects on ground of prior use or has withdrawn such refusal or has notified a grant of protection, it may, if its legislation permits, grant a defined period as specified in the Regulations for terminating such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows third parties time to terminate pre-existing uses; Contracting Party must notify International Bureau of the period (Article 17(1)-(2); Rule 14 further specifies limits and notification details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of grant of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Competent Authority of a Contracting Party may notify the International Bureau of the grant of protection to a registered appellation of origin or geographical indication; the International Bureau shall record and publish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizes when a Contracting Party affirms protection following international registration (Article 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation — opportunity to defend and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation of the effects, in part or in whole, of an international registration in the territory of a Contracting Party may be pronounced only after having given the beneficiaries an opportunity to defend their rights; Contracting Party shall notify International Bureau which shall record and publish the invalidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process guarantee for beneficiaries; invalidation entries are published and do not prejudice other protections (Article 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications and other entries procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for modification of international registrations and other entries in the International Register shall be specified in the Regulations; permissible modifications include addition/deletion of beneficiaries, changes of names/addresses, modification of limits of geographical area, changes related to legislative/administrative/judicial acts, and certain Contracting Party changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 15 enumerates permissible modifications and requires Competent Authority (or beneficiaries in Article 5(3) cases) to present requests with fees; International Bureau enters modifications and notifies other Competent Authorities (Article 20; Rule 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership and Assembly participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Parties shall be members of the same Special Union as States party to the Lisbon Agreement/1967 Act; each Contracting Party shall be represented in the Assembly by one delegate (assisted by alternates/advisors/experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational governance: representation, expenses borne by delegations, and integration with Assembly of the 1967 Act parties (Article 21-22(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly tasks and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall deal with maintenance and development of the Special Union and implementation of the Act, give directions concerning revision conferences, amend the Regulations, review/approve Director General reports, determine program and budget, adopt financial Regulations, establish committees/working groups, and adopt amendments to Articles 22-24 and 27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly is the principal decision-making organ for policy, Regulations, budget, and institutional arrangements (Article 22(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum, decision-making, and voting rules in Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: One-half of members with right to vote constitute quorum for a vote; where representation is between one-third and one-half of States, decisions may be taken but will take effect only if absent members provide written votes/abstentions within three months; Assembly endeavors to decide by consensus, otherwise voting rules apply (each State one vote; intergovernmental organizations vote with number equal to member States), and decisions generally require two-thirds of votes cast unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed quorum/majority mechanics (Article 22(3)-(5)); certain Articles require special majorities (see Article 27). Abstentions not counted as votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau roles and Director General responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: International registration and related duties, and all other administrative tasks concerning the Special Union, shall be performed by the International Bureau; the Director General is Chief Executive of the Special Union, prepares meetings, represents Special Union, and participates without vote in meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau handles registrations, publications, records, Secretariat functions, and preparatory work for revision conferences; Director General establishes Administrative Instructions (Article 23; Rule 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance sources, budget and fee-fixing
rubrics_metrics.description: Income of the Special Union derives from fees collected under Article 7, proceeds from publications, gifts/bequests, rent/investment revenue, and special contributions; amounts of fees fixed by Assembly on proposal of Director General so revenue should normally cover expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeting and fee-setting are institutional tasks of Assembly; classes of contribution correspond to Paris Convention classes; working capital fund and host State advances mechanisms exist (Article 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations: details and amendment constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The details for carrying out this Act shall be established in the Regulations; the Assembly may decide that certain provisions of the Regulations may be amended only by unanimity or a three-fourths majority; in case of conflict, the Act prevails over Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations contain procedural specifics; Assembly can restrict amendment routes for particular Regulation provisions; Act supersedes Regulations (Article 25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and amendment procedures for the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act may be revised by Diplomatic Conferences; Articles 22-24 and 27 may be amended either by revision conference or by the Assembly according to Article 27; proposals for amendment must be communicated six months in advance; specified majorities (three-fourths or four-fifths) are required for adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal constitutional amendment/revision mechanics including proposal, notice, majority thresholds and entry-into-force rules (Articles 26-27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of invalidation — required particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: When effects of an international registration are invalidated and the invalidation is no longer subject to appeal, the Competent Authority shall transmit a notification to the International Bureau indicating the registration number, authority pronouncing invalidation, date, particulars if partial, grounds, and a copy of decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau enters invalidation in Register and communicates to Competent Authority of Origin/beneficiaries (Rule 13(1)-(2)). Required to ensure record completeness and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of transitional period — contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a third party is granted a defined period to terminate use (Article 17(1)), Competent Authority shall notify the International Bureau indicating registration number, identity of third party, period granted and scope of use, and the date from which period begins; the start date may not be later than one year and three months from receipt of notification of international registration (or two years and three months in certain Article 29(4) cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 14 limits duration: not longer than 15 years; periods longer than 10 years would be exceptional. International Bureau enters notification and communicates to Competent Authority of Origin/beneficiaries when notified timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible modifications that can be recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications that may be recorded include: (i) addition/deletion of beneficiary(ies); (ii) change of beneficiaries' names/addresses; (iii) modification of limits of geographical area of origin; (iv) modification relating to the legislative/administrative/judicial act or registration under which protection was granted; (v) modification relating to the Contracting Party of Origin not affecting geographical area; (vi) modification under Rule 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure requires Competent Authority (or beneficiaries in Article 5(3) cases) to present request with fee; International Bureau enters modifications with date and notifies other Competent Authorities (Rule 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation of protection and withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent Authority of Contracting Party of Origin or beneficiaries or relevant entities may notify the International Bureau at any time that protection is renounced in whole or in part in respect of one or some Contracting Parties; any renunciation may be withdrawn at any time subject to payment of modification fee and correction of irregularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renunciation/withdrawal entries are recorded and communicated to Competent Authorities; withdrawal of renunciation may trigger opportunity for other Competent Authorities to refuse effects within one year (Rule 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation request procedure and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for cancellation shall state the number of the international registration (and other identity details); International Bureau shall enter cancellation in Register, confirm entry to Contracting Party of Origin (or beneficiaries) and inform other Competent Authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation can be requested by Competent Authority of Origin or beneficiaries (Rule 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to the International Register and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau finds an error ex officio or at request of Competent Authority of Origin, it shall correct the Register; beneficiaries may be notified of corrections; where correction concerns appellation/indication or goods, a Competent Authority may declare inability to ensure protection within one year and Rules 9 to 12 apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are communicated to all Competent Authorities; corrections affecting substantive fields may permit Contracting Parties to refuse protection within defined time (Rule 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Register entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall publish all entries made in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication ensures transparency and is carried out without delay for registrations, refusals, modifications, invalidations, cancellations, etc. (Rule 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of extracts and documents by International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts from the International Register or any other information shall be provided by the International Bureau to any person requesting on payment of the fee; any person may request a copy in the original language of the provisions/decisions/registration under which a denomination is protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If International Bureau does not have a document it will request it from Competent Authority of Origin; fees for extracts/copies are set in Rule 8/Regulations (Rule 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of signature and authenticated communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the signature of a Competent Authority is required under these Regulations, such signature may be printed or replaced by affixing a facsimile or an official seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates administrative communications and filings by permitting facsimile/printed signatures and seals (Rule 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of dispatch rules for postal and other communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where notifications are communicated through postal service, date of dispatch is determined by the postmark; if postmark is illegible/missing International Bureau treats as if sent 20 days before receipt; for mail delivery services date is based on delivery service information; notifications may also be by facsimile or electronic means as in Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes objective dispatch dates to calculate deadlines; parties should use traceable means of communication to fix dates (Rule 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of notification by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications (of registration, withdrawal of renunciation, etc.) shall be addressed by any means enabling the International Bureau to establish the date on which the notification was received, as provided in Administrative Instructions; other notifications must be addressed by any means enabling the International Bureau to establish receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes use of communication methods that record receipt dates (Rule 23). Administrative Instructions provide detailed permitted modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Instructions — establishment, consultation and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall establish Administrative Instructions and may modify them, after consulting Competent Authorities with direct interest; Administrative Instructions deal with matters expressly referred to them by the Regulations and with details for application; the Assembly may invite the Director General to modify any provision and the Director General shall act upon invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions supply operational detail (e.g., electronic communications, forms, formats); they must be published with effective dates and cannot conflict with Act or Regulations (Rule 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and precedence of Administrative Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Instructions and any modification shall be published and specify the date on which they become effective; in case of conflict between Administrative Instructions and the Act or Regulations, the latter prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency of procedural guidance and preserves hierarchical legal supremacy (Rule 24(3)-(4)).
